line: Crowley's Knight of Swords: the Yodh of the Name, the fiery part of Air, and a span from Taurus to Gemini.

sections.title: The court and its element
sections.line: Crowley names the Knights by the powers of the letter Yodh in the Name.

quotes.quote: The Knights represent the powers of the letter Yodh in the Name.
The Knight of Swords represents the fiery part of Air; he is the wind, the storm.

sections.title: Its span in the Zodiac
sections.line: The text gives the 21st degree of Taurus as the start and the 20th of Gemini as the end. Crowley's attribution table (pdf p274) gives 20 degrees at both ends. The page follows the text, and the table's figures are not quoted.

quotes.quote: He rules from the 21st degree of Taurus to the 20th degree of Gemini.
instead of assigning the three decans of each sign to one card, the influence begins with the last decan of one Sign and continues to the second decan of the next.
It might well be expected that the elemental attribution would harmonize with the Zodiacal attribution; but it is not so.

sections.title: Its character as Crowley describes it
sections.line: Crowley's description of the figure and the card, in his own words.

quotes.quote: The moral qualities of a person thus indicated are activity and skill, subtlety and cleverness.
